problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(4,0).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$
worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies on the positive half of the $x$-axis, we have $\theta =0.$ 

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(4,0).$
